question: What architectural patterns let an agentic system generate, evaluate and learn from its own outputs while staying safe, affordable and accountable?
contributions: R5 operational model (Relax, Reflect, Reference, Retry, Report)

Patterns: Hybrid Planner+Scorer, Custom Evaluation Metrics, Preference-Controlled Synthetic Data Generation, Advanced Model Tuning (SFT/PEFT, DPO), Coevolved Agent Training, Adversarial Testing and Red Teaming, Cost Management and Tokenomics, Measuring Business Value (ROI)

limits: No experiments, benchmarks or measured results: every number is an illustration or an uncited assertion.
No reference list; Reflexion, SelfCheckGPT, lost-in-the-middle, DPO, LoRA, TRL, BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore/BLEURT are named without citation.
Prose and code disagree in several places (see problems): code is stub scaffolding, not an implementation of the described behaviour.
PEFT/SFT 'pseudocode' promised on p382-383 is absent from the PDF.
'Exponential improvement' from co-evolution is asserted with no evidence; the chapter itself names runaway divergence and collusion as failure modes.
Synthetic data caveats conceded: amplifies generator bias, lacks edge-case diversity; DPO can overfit and worsen hallucination (p379, p383).
practices: Separate the generator (planner) from the evaluator (scorer) rather than have one agent grade itself; start with a simple scoring rubric as the contract between them (p370-374).
Build custom, domain-specific metrics against a golden dataset with domain experts; begin rule-based and refine (p375-378).
Create preference pairs by controlling one variable (e.g. RAG context quality) so one output is reliably better; beware bias amplification and missing edge cases (p378-382).
Use SFT/PEFT (LoRA) for domain knowledge or format, DPO for preference alignment; DPO can overfit narrow preference patterns (p382-383).
Retrain in batches large enough to be statistically significant and cost-effective, not after every output; ground co-evolution with periodic human review or a golden dataset (p385, p389).
Run a red-team agent continuously against the production agent; log successful attacks and patch system prompt or fine-tune data; use jailbreak ensembles and multi-agent attacks (p389-392).
Give each agent a token/dollar budget with a circuit breaker; tag cloud resources; alert at a percentage of budget; per-agent quotas (p393-396).
Report business KPIs (time-to-decision, cost-per-task, human escalation, uptime, intervention rate, safety violations) not only accuracy; start with one or two metrics (p397-400).
Balance exploitation and exploration in the Learn stage to avoid local optima (p368).

terms.definition: a conceptual model that illustrates this continuous, four-stage cycle: Generate, Evaluate, Learn, Deploy
Relax (manage context and latency), Reflect (checkpoints and self-critique), Reference (provenance), Retry (adaptive error handling), Report (quantify factuality, consistency, process quality)
two distinct agent roles: a planner (generator) producing candidates and a scorer (evaluator) that only scores or ranks them
custom workflow metric: step recall, precision, and a penalty for out-of-order steps against a golden guide
generate chosen/rejected pairs under controlled conditions (e.g. rich vs poor context) so one is demonstrably better, to train a scorer via DPO
planner and scorer trained together, each pushing the other; failure modes runaway divergence and collusion
the planner learns to game the system, producing low-quality outputs that exploit biases or blind spots in the scorer
the system progressively drifts from the actual business objective to optimize an internal proxy metric

lineage.note: lightweight verbal self-feedback as driver of improvement
sampling for stochastic consistency as reliability metric
tuning method for planner and scorer; no citation
called logic-blind, insufficient for agentic workflows

code.snippet: score = len(solution)  # 'Simple scoring rubric: score based on length.'
order_penalty += 0.1  # position-wise mismatch; final_score = f1_score - order_penalty; return max(0, final_score)

problems: PROSE vs CODE: planner/scorer example (p372) says scorer ranks on brand voice and predicted click-through rate and the ranking fine-tunes the planner; code (p373) scores by len(solution), returns hard-coded slogans, and has no feedback or tuning step.

PROSE vs CODE: STEPScore prose says percentage of required steps (recall) and relevant steps (precision) plus a penalty for out-of-order steps; code uses set-based F1 (order-blind) and a positional-mismatch penalty of 0.1 per index, so a missing middle step is also penalised as disorder; book prints no outputs (reader's calculation: 1.00, 0.80, 0.70).

PROSE vs CODE: p379 says synthetic pairs train the scorer via DPO; the DPO snippet (p383) loads 'my-sft-planner-agent' and imports AutoModelForCausalLMWithValueHead, i.e. trains a planner policy; DPO also does not by itself produce a scorer. Chapter says DPO avoids full RL, but orchestrator (p388) calls tune_planner_with_rl and Fig 11.5 says 'via RL/DPO'.
PROSE vs CODE: preference-pair code (p381) is a string template with 'HIGHLY RELEVANT' keyword check; pair is trivially separable, so it demonstrates labelling, not any quality learning.

PROSE vs CODE: cost example says $50.00 per job with circuit breaker at 90% on the 50th PDF (p394); code says monthly_budget $50, trips only when spend > budget (100%), no 90% alert. Walking the code: $7 before job, job logs 5M ($10) -> $17, then 20M ($40) -> $57, second job blocked.

PROSE vs CODE: ROI example (p398) computes cost savings vs human baseline ($0.50 vs $12.00, $45,000); code (p399) never computes savings, defines 'impact_correlation' as satisfaction / success_rate (a ratio), over two days, and prints 'A clear positive correlation is observed' unconditionally.
Red-team code (p391) blocks the attack by string-matching 'reveal your system prompt', so the test passes by construction.
Coevolution orchestrator (p387-388) is all commented stubs returning empty lists; it prints step messages only.
Missing content: p382 promises PEFT/SFT pseudocode; none appears on p382-383 (the page has no code or image).
Duplicated text: the 'advanced patterns provide the high-level architecture for implementing R5' paragraph appears twice (p370) and the closing roadmap paragraph twice (p400-401).

DPO snippet API: passes tokenizer= and beta= directly to DPOTrainer and uses a value-head model; newer TRL versions use DPOConfig and processing_class (reader knowledge, flagged as not from the text). Snippet is labelled non-runnable.

Invented worked-example numbers: $0.002/1k tokens, $50 budget, 5M/1M/2.5M/20M token logs, 5,000 PDFs, 50th PDF, 90%, $0.50 vs $12.00, $45,000, 92% intent recognition, <2 s latency, 1500/1600 tasks, 0.92/0.94, 1200/1350 tickets, CSAT 4.1/4.3, STEPScore 0.1 penalty, DPO beta 0.1, Fig 11.3 score 0.85, Fig 11.8 KPI -20%/+10%. The 10x-100x multiplier is an uncited assertion.
